meta.title: Common Ground
meta.subtitle: Australian federal party policies, side by side — every claim sourced
meta.disclaimer: Independent, non-partisan summary. Positions are paraphrased from the cited public sources and may change; always check the linked source. Not affiliated with any political party.
meta.methodology: Positions were researched from official party platforms, government/minister media releases, legislation and reputable news outlets, then independently verified: every cited source was fetched and checked to confirm it supports the stated position. Positions that could not be verified against a working source are shown as 'No clear position'.

issues.label: Negative gearing reform
issues.question: Should negative gearing and the capital gains tax discount for property investors be restricted?

positions.summary: Labor has ruled out changes to negative gearing and the CGT discount this term, keeping current investor tax settings.
positions.impact_note: Investor tax settings stay as they are; no change for landlords or buyers competing with investors.

sources.title: PM rules out negative gearing changes

positions.summary: The Coalition opposes any restriction of negative gearing or the CGT discount, describing them as standard investment deductions.
positions.impact_note: Property investors keep existing tax deductions; no change to rental market settings.

positions.summary: The Greens want negative gearing and the CGT discount phased out for investors with more than one property, redirecting savings to public housing.
positions.impact_note: Fewer tax breaks for multi-property investors; intended to cool investor demand and fund public homes.

positions.summary: No clear verified position on negative gearing reform was found in recent statements or platform documents.
positions.impact_note: Unclear what would change for renters or investors.

issues.label: Bulk-billing expansion
issues.question: Should Medicare bulk-billing incentives be expanded to cover most GP visits?

positions.summary: Labor is funding expanded bulk-billing incentives for all Medicare card holders, aiming for 9 in 10 GP visits to be free by 2030.
positions.impact_note: More GP visits with no out-of-pocket fee, depending on whether your clinic takes up the incentive.

positions.summary: The Coalition matched Labor's bulk-billing incentive expansion during the 2025 campaign and has maintained support for the funding.
positions.impact_note: Same practical effect: cheaper GP visits where clinics take up the incentive.

positions.summary: The Greens support expanded bulk billing and want to go further, pushing to include dental and mental health in Medicare.
positions.impact_note: Free GP visits plus a push to make dentist and psychology visits Medicare-funded too.

positions.summary: One Nation supports Medicare in principle but has criticised the cost of the incentive package without opposing it outright.
positions.impact_note: Position unclear in practice; has not blocked the funding in the Senate.
